::: {.lead}
**ECO2101 — Macroeconomic Theory II.** The fourth quarter of the PhD first-year
macroeconomics sequence at the University of Toronto, Winter 2026. The course
builds up heterogeneous-agent macroeconomics from dynamic programming through
firm dynamics and aggregate risk to sequence-space Jacobian methods, following
recent papers and two open-access textbooks.
:::

<h2 class="section-head">Lectures</h2>

<ol class="pub-list">

<li>
<span class="pub-title">Introduction to Modern Macroeconomics</span>
<span class="pub-note">What a modern macro model specifies — the stochastic dynamic environment, equilibrium and recursion — and why balanced growth restricts admissible preferences.</span>
<span class="pub-links"><a class="pub-link" href="/files/ECO2101_Dyrda_Lecture1.pdf">Slides</a></span>
</li>

<li>
<span class="pub-title">Dynamic Programming I: Fixed Points, Contractions, and Optimal Stopping</span>
<span class="pub-note">Fixed-point theory, contraction mappings and Markov dynamics, developed throughout on a firm with stochastic productivity. Threshold policies, monotonicity and continuation values.</span>
<span class="pub-links"><a class="pub-link" href="/files/ECO2101_Dyrda_Lecture2.pdf">Slides</a></span>
</li>

<li>
<span class="pub-title">Dynamic Programming II: Efficient Algorithms for the Household Problem</span>
<span class="pub-note">Markov decision processes and the VFI / HPI / OPI family, endogenous gridpoints and envelope conditions, and discrete–continuous choice with extreme-value shocks.</span>
<span class="pub-links"><a class="pub-link" href="/files/ECO2101_Dyrda_Lecture3.pdf">Slides</a></span>
</li>

<li>
<span class="pub-title">Firm Dynamics: Entry, Exit, and Misallocation</span>
<span class="pub-note">Hopenhayn (1992) on entry, exit and long-run equilibrium, with the computational procedure worked through; then Hopenhayn and Rogerson (1993) on nonconvex adjustment costs, inaction regions and their aggregate consequences.</span>
<span class="pub-links"><a class="pub-link" href="/files/ECO2101_Dyrda_Lecture4.pdf">Slides</a></span>
</li>

<li>
<span class="pub-title">Entrepreneurship and Financial Frictions</span>
<span class="pub-note">The canonical occupational-choice model — Aiyagari with entrepreneurs and collateral constraints — followed by Quadrini (2000), Buera and Shin (2013), and Moll (2014) on whether self-financing undoes misallocation.</span>
<span class="pub-links"><a class="pub-link" href="/files/ECO2101_Dyrda_Lecture5.pdf">Slides</a></span>
</li>

<li>
<span class="pub-title">Aggregate Risk in Heterogeneous Agent Economies</span>
<span class="pub-note">Krusell and Smith (1998): the distribution as a state variable, bounded-rationality forecasting rules, approximate aggregation, and the computational algorithm.</span>
<span class="pub-links"><a class="pub-link" href="/files/ECO2101_Dyrda_Lecture6.pdf">Slides</a></span>
</li>

<li>
<span class="pub-title">Aggregate Risk in Heterogeneous Agent Economies: Applications</span>
<span class="pub-note">Three tests of when and why heterogeneity matters for aggregates: lumpy investment (Khan and Thomas, 2008), credit shocks (Khan and Thomas, 2013), and uncertainty shocks (Bloom et al., 2018).</span>
<span class="pub-links"><a class="pub-link" href="/files/ECO2101_Dyrda_Lecture7.pdf">Slides</a></span>
</li>

<li>
<span class="pub-title">Sequence-Space Jacobians</span>
<span class="pub-note">Auclert, Bardóczy, Rognlie and Straub (2021): writing equilibrium as H(K, Z) = 0 in the sequence space, impulse responses from a single matrix, and certainty equivalence as a consequence of linearization rather than an assumption.</span>
<span class="pub-links"><a class="pub-link" href="/files/ECO2101_Dyrda_Lecture8.pdf">Slides</a></span>
</li>

<li>
<span class="pub-title">Sequence-Space Jacobians II: The Fake News Algorithm, DAGs, and HANK</span>
<span class="pub-note">Computing the Jacobians efficiently via the fake news algorithm, composing blocks along a directed acyclic graph, and an application to one-asset HANK.</span>
<span class="pub-links"><a class="pub-link" href="/files/ECO2101_Dyrda_Lecture9.pdf">Slides</a></span>
</li>

</ol>
